To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Multidisciplinary rehabilitation and progressive exercises improved physical impairment, low back pain intensity and health related quality of level, but not sickness absence.”

the multidisciplinary rehabilitation and progressive exercises are effective for improving health related quality of Life, reducing LBP and physical impairment, but not effective in reducing the sickness absence of non-acute, moderately painful LBP in the occupational health care setting.

the multidisciplinary intervention was more effective than the control group in reducing low back pain intensity and improving physical impairment and health related quality of level at 2 years follow-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effectiveness of three different interventions in reducing low back pain (and associated symptoms) in employees.
the development of a novel approach for the analysis of data from randomized trials with a natural history control.
the effectiveness of three non-surgical interventions in the occupational health care setting for secondary prevention of moderate non-acute low-back pain (LBP).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the multidisciplinary rehabilitation and the progressive exercises interventions were effective in improving health related quality of the life, decreasing low back pain and decreasing physical impairment in non acute, moderate low back pain.
the interventions were effective for reducing low back pain and disability in non-acute low-back pain, but not for reducing sickness absence.
the interventions improved health-related quality of life and decreased pain and physical impairment, but not sickness absence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rehab intervention was effective in improving LBP, health related quality of Life, and physical impairment, whereas the Advice group was not effective compared to the Control group.
the Rehab and Physio interventions had positive effects on health-related quality of life and physical impairment, and the Physio intervention also had positive effects on pain.
the interventions were effective in improving the health related quality of low back pain and decreasing pain and physical impairment, but not in sickness absence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multidisciplinary rehabilitation and exercise interventions were effective in improving health related quality of the life and reducing pain intensity in non-acute LBP.
the interventions were effective on reducing LBP and physical impairment.

we found evidence for effectiveness of multidisciplinary rehabilitation or progressive exercise in improving health related quality of live, decreasing pain intensity and physical impairment, but we found little evidence of effectiveness of self-care advice in non-acute moderate low back pain.
